title: Natural isomorphisms of prescribed raw bilinear scalar extensions
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $C$ an $R$-linear preadditive category and $D$ an $S$-linear preadditive category. Choose $t\in R$, $b\in S$ and any function $c:R[1/t]\to S[1/b]$. Use raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], with scalar-first tensor notation for Hom. Let $U,V:C\times C\to D$ be functors and $e:U\cong V$. Let $F,G:C[1/t]\times C[1/t]\to D[1/b]$ have the literal objects $U,V$, respectively. Assume, for every four input objects, that their maps are given by biadditive maps of the two localized Hom groups, whose values on pure tensors are $F(x\otimes f,y\otimes g)=c(xy)\otimes U(f,g)$ and $G(x\otimes f,y\otimes g)=c(xy)\otimes V(f,g)$ under the prescribed object equalities. There is exactly one natural isomorphism $F\cong G$ whose component is the scalar-localization image of the component of $e$, interpreted through those object equalities. No ring-homomorphism assumption on $c$ is added.

proof.text: Conjugate the localized integral isomorphism components by the given object equalities. Tensor induction in the first and then the second input arrow reduces naturality to zero, sums and pure tensors. The first two cases follow from additivity. In the pure case the two prescribed formulas and the scalar-localization composition formula reduce the equation to integral naturality, with the common scalar c(xy). Use NatIso.ofComponents. Component extensionality proves uniqueness. This is the existing complete private proof, retained verbatim apart from its public name and namespace.

theorem existsUnique
    {R : Type r} [CommRing R] {S : Type s} [CommRing S]
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Preadditive C] [Linear R C]
    {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] [Linear S D]
    (t : R) (b : S) (c : Localization.Away t → Localization.Away b)
    (U V : C × C ⥤ D) (e : U ≅ V)
    (F G : ScalarLocalization R C t × ScalarLocalization R C t ⥤
      ScalarLocalization S D b)
    (hF : ∀ K, F.obj K = ⟨U.obj (K.1.obj, K.2.obj)⟩)
    (hG : ∀ K, G.obj K = ⟨V.obj (K.1.obj, K.2.obj)⟩)
    (mF : ∀ (K K' L L' : ScalarLocalization R C t),
      ∃ β : (K ⟶ K') →+
        (L ⟶ L') →+ (F.obj (K, L) ⟶ F.obj (K', L')),
        (∀ f g, F.map (Prod.mkHom f g) = β f g) ∧
        ∀ (f : K.obj ⟶ K'.obj) (g : L.obj ⟶ L'.obj) (x y : Localization.Away t),
          HEq (β (x ⊗ₜ[R] f) (y ⊗ₜ[R] g))
            (c (x * y) ⊗ₜ[S] U.map (Prod.mkHom f g)))
    (mG : ∀ (K K' L L' : ScalarLocalization R C t),
      ∃ β : (K ⟶ K') →+
        (L ⟶ L') →+ (G.obj (K, L) ⟶ G.obj (K', L')),
        (∀ f g, G.map (Prod.mkHom f g) = β f g) ∧
        ∀ (f : K.obj ⟶ K'.obj) (g : L.obj ⟶ L'.obj) (x y : Localization.Away t),
          HEq (β (x ⊗ₜ[R] f) (y ⊗ₜ[R] g))
            (c (x * y) ⊗ₜ[S] V.map (Prod.mkHom f g))) :
    ∃! α : F ≅ G, ∀ K, HEq (α.hom.app K)
      ((ScalarLocalization.localization S D b).map (e.hom.app (K.1.obj, K.2.obj)))
